build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player progresses car-by-car through a procedurally generated train. Each car is a self-contained encounter that resolves before moving to the next. The train layout is different each run. Score 0 if no car-by-car progression exists.

Combat is turn-based with cover mechanics — the bandit and enemies take positions behind furniture and exchange fire. Cover reduces incoming damage. Positioning matters tactically. Score 0 if no combat exists.

Ammo is limited and must be looted from fallen guards or found in cars. Running out of ammo forces melee or retreat. The ammo counter is visible and creates resource tension. Score 0 if ammo is unlimited or no ammo system exists.

A turn counter represents distance to the station. If it reaches zero before the player reaches the engine, the heist fails. The counter decreases each car or turn, creating forward pressure. Score 0 if no time pressure exists.

Reaching the engine triggers a boss fight against the conductor with unique mechanics. Victory and defeat both have distinct result screens showing run performance. Score 0 if no boss or ending exists.

At least 5 distinct car types exist: passenger (robbery choices), guard (combat), cargo (locked safes), dining (cover shootout), mail (timed vault). Each resolves through different interactions. Score 0 if fewer than 3 car types exist.

Passenger cars offer robbery choices: intimidate for quick cash or search thoroughly for better loot but risk alerting guards ahead. Choices have observable consequences in later cars. Score 0 if no meaningful choices exist.
A black-market car appears mid-train offering health kits, ammo, special weapons, and disguises for purchase with looted gold. At least 4 purchasable item types exist. Score 0 if no shop car exists.
At least 3 distinct enemy types exist (guards with pistols, shotgun guards, armored guards, guard dogs) with different combat behaviors and cover usage. Score 0 if only one enemy type exists.

Victory shows total loot, cars cleared, turns remaining, and enemies defeated. Failure shows how far along the train the bandit reached and loot collected before death/timeout. Score 0 if no results exist.
A styled title screen shows a steam train silhouette against a sunset with the game name. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The game flow connects title -> train overview -> car encounters -> shop -> boss -> results without restarting. A progress bar shows position along the train. Score 0 if transitions are missing.
During encounters, health, ammo count, turn counter, loot collected, and cover positions are clearly visible. Enemy health and positions are shown. Score 0 if no combat display exists.
Readability at 1280x720 is strong: the bandit, enemies, cover objects, car interiors, and loot are all clearly distinguishable. Score 0 if elements blend together.

The art direction is coherent across title, train cars, combat, characters, and UI — a consistent western/heist aesthetic with warm dusty palette. Score 0 if mostly default UI or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Train car interiors have distinct illustrated art per car type (plush passenger seats, cargo crates, dining tables). Characters have sprite art. Cover objects are visually clear. Score 0 if all cars look identical or use plain fills.

HUD and UI chrome: health/ammo display, turn counter, progress bar, shop interface, and result screens use styled themed widgets — not raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled.

Animation and feedback: gunfire has muzzle flash and impact effects, cover shows bullet impacts, enemies react to hits, the train sways or scrolls in the background, and car transitions have door-opening animations. Score 0 if all state changes snap silently.
